name: NEMO telescope
summary: An Italian deep-sea neutrino-telescope R&D programme tested tower structures and marine infrastructure that preceded the Italian KM3NeT site.
detection_principle: Optical modules on connected rigid tower arms measured Cherenkov light in seawater. Acoustic positioning, timing calibration and shore connections demonstrated systems needed for a larger telescope.
technologies: Acoustic background monitoring with the ONDE hydrophone prototype

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: INFN-LNS explicitly reports the Phase-2 operating interval; later large-telescope construction belongs to KM3NeT.

timeline.event: Phase-2 tower deployed at Capo Passero.

collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Phase-2 tower
key_parameters.value: Eight floors and 32 optical modules; approximately 380 m tall

phases.name: NEMO-ONDE acoustic demonstrator
phases.description: Four hydrophones deployed 25 km offshore Catania at 2,000 m depth in January 2005 operated for about two years; 30 Hz–43 kHz acoustic-background monitoring supported neutrino-detection feasibility and marine biology. It did not claim acoustic neutrino detection.

results.summary: The Phase-1 prototype reconstructed atmospheric-muon flux.
Phase-2 documented long-term deep-water optical background and its environmental dependence.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
